Name: Batch Processor
Author: Skyking2020
Description:
[heading]Description[/heading]
Batch Processor is a quality-of-life mod that lets many of Stardew Valley's processing machines handle entire stacks instead of making you feed them the same item over and over... and over... and over.

The goal is simple: [b]remove repetitive clicking without changing how the machines actually work.[/b]

Each item is still processed as its own job, at the normal processing speed, using Stardew Valley's normal machine logic. Machines with randomized outputs still roll their output normally for every individual cycle.

Load up a machine, go farm, fish, mine, sleep, question your life choices while reorganizing your chests for the sixth time, and come back later.

Batch Processor handles the clicking. Stardew handles everything else.
[line]
[heading]Main Features[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Process full stacks[/b] - Put a stack of up to 999 valid items into a supported machine with one interaction.[/*]
[*][b]Vanilla processing speed[/b] - Batching doesn't make machines faster. Every job still takes its normal amount of time.[/*]
[*][b]Vanilla output RNG[/b] - Machines with randomized results still determine their output separately for every processing cycle.[/*]
[*][b]Collect while processing[/b] - Finished items can be collected while the rest of the batch continues.[/*]
[*][b]Works while you're away[/b] - Batches continue while you're in another location or sleeping.[/*]
[*][b]Handles multi-item recipes[/b] - Machines that normally require several items per cycle still consume the correct amount.[/*]
[*][b]Handles only one item type at a time[/b] - You cannot mix items. For instance, if you have copper in a furnace, you cannot throw iron on top of it.[/*]
[*][b]No additions [/b]- You can't add more items while the machine is working.[/*]
[*][b]No speed boosts. No free items. No RNG manipulation. No balance changes.[/b][/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]Supported Machines[/heading]
Batch Processor currently supports [b]15 machines[/b]:
[list]
[*][b]Seed Maker[/b][/*]
[*][b]Keg[/b][/*]
[*][b]Furnace[/b][/*]
[*][b]Preserves Jar[/b][/*]
[*][b]Cheese Press[/b][/*]
[*][b]Mayonnaise Machine[/b][/*]
[*][b]Loom[/b][/*]
[*][b]Oil Maker[/b][/*]
[*][b]Recycling Machine[/b][/*]
[*][b]Bone Mill[/b][/*]
[*][b]Charcoal Kiln[/b][/*]
[*][b]Slime Egg-Press[/b][/*]
[*][b]Geode Crusher[/b][/*]
[*][b]Dehydrator[/b][/*]
[*][b]Fish Smoker[/b][/*]
[/list]Machines that require multiple items for a single processing cycle still follow their normal recipe. For example, the Furnace processes ore in groups of 5, the Charcoal Kiln uses 10 Wood, and the Slime Egg-Press uses 100 Slime.
Leftovers that don't make a complete recipe stay with you.
[line]
[heading]Machines Not Affected[/heading]
Some machines are intentionally left alone because batching them would either change their fundamental behavior or require Batch Processor to invent rules that don't exist in vanilla Stardew Valley.

[list]
[*][b]Casks[/b] are excluded because they age a single item through multiple quality stages and allow the player to remove that item early. A batch queue would have to decide when one item is "finished," which would change how Casks work.[/*]
[*][b]Crystalariums[/b] are excluded because they continuously reproduce the inserted mineral rather than consuming a stack of inputs.[/*]
[*][b]Incubators and Ostrich Incubators[/b] are excluded because they're growth/incubation systems, not stack-processing machines.[/*]
[*][b]Tappers and Heavy Tappers[/b] are excluded because they passively produce items from trees rather than consuming input items.[/*]
[*][b]Bee Houses[/b] are excluded because they passively produce Honey.[/*]
[*][b]Worm Bins and Deluxe Worm Bins[/b] are excluded because they're passive producers rather than input processors.[/*]
[*][b]Mushroom Logs[/b] are excluded because their production is based on their environment and nearby trees rather than processing a stack of player-supplied items.[/*]
[*][b]Bait Makers[/b] are intentionally excluded. Their output contains information about the specific fish used to create the targeted bait, making them considerably funkier than a normal input → output processor. Sometimes it's better not to poke the weird machine.[/*]
[*][b]Heavy Furnaces[/b] are also intentionally excluded and retain their normal vanilla behavior.[/*]
[*]In general, if a machine [b]ages, grows, incubates, duplicates, or passively produces something[/b], Batch Processor leaves it alone.[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]⚠ A Note About Removing Machines[/heading]
Batch Processor doesn't add special protection when you use an axe, pickaxe, or other normal method to remove a processing machine.
If you remove a machine while it contains an active batch or uncollected output, [b]you may lose the items stored in that machine. So wait for the batch to finish.[/b]
[line]
[heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install [b]SMAPI[/b].[/*]
[*]Download [b]Batch Processor[/b].[/*]
[*]Extract the
[code]BatchProcessor[/code]folder into your Stardew Valley
[code]Mods[/code]folder.[/*]
[*]Launch Stardew Valley through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]That's it.
There is no configuration required. Install it and start feeding stacks into supported machines.
[line]
[heading]Uninstallation[/heading]
Remove the
[code]BatchProcessor[/code]folder from your Stardew Valley
[code]Mods[/code]folder.
For the safest uninstall, finish or collect any active batches before removing the mod.
[line]
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0 or later[/b][/*]
[/list]
